title: fix(app-shell,components): Setup-app UX — accurate teams empty state + stop form prop leak
body:
Two defects surfaced by a system-settings (Setup) app review.

## 1. Empty-state / CTA mismatch on `sys_team`

The Teams list showed the generic better-auth empty state — *"These records are created by the authentication provider … not added by hand here"* — directly beside a working **Create Team** button. The copy flatly contradicted the affordance.

Root cause: `resolveManagedByEmptyState` hard-codes the "not added by hand" disclaimer for every `better-auth` object except `sys_user`, ignoring that `sys_team` has a `create_team` toolbar action. Fix: give teams their own accurate copy (they can be created here, or arrive via org/SSO provisioning), mirroring the existing `sys_user` special case. (`app-shell/utils/managedByEmptyState.ts` + en/zh i18n)

## 2. Form props leaking onto the DOM

Every object **list view** logged:
- `React does not recognize the 'objectName' prop on a DOM element`
- `Unknown event handler property 'onDirtyChange'. It will be ignored.`

Root cause: the form renderer spreads leftover top-level props onto its `<form>` element and its DOM-safe strip list was missing `objectName` / `onDirtyChange` (and other FormSchema-only props). Fix: extend the strip list. (`components/renderers/form/form.tsx`)

## Verification

- Unit: `managedByEmptyState.test.ts` (new `sys_team` guard) and the form renderer suite pass.
- Browser (live backend): the Teams list now renders **"No teams yet — create one with Create Team…"** next to a working Create Team button; navigating object list views logs **zero** prop-leak warnings (verified via a `console.error` capture — 0 hits).
